package q27331;
import java.util.*;
class QuadraticEquation{
public static void main(String[] args){
	Scanner sc= new Scanner(System.in);
		System.out.print("Coefficient a: ");
	double a=sc.nextDouble();
	System.out.print("Coefficient b: ");
	double b=sc.nextDouble();
	System.out.print("Coefficient c: ");
	double c=sc.nextDouble();
	double d=b*b-4*a*c;
	if(d>0){
		System.out.println("The roots are real and distinct");
		double root1,root2;
		root1=((-b)+Math.sqrt(d))/(2*a);
		root2=((-b)-Math.sqrt(d))/(2*a);
		System.out.println("Root1: "+root1+ " Root2: "+root2);
	}
	else if(d==0){
		double root;
		System.out.println("The roots are real and equal");
		root=-b/(2*a);
		System.out.println("Root: "+root);
	}
	else{
		System.out.println("The roots are imaginary");
	}
}
}

package q17128;
import java.util.Scanner;
public class CTJ17128 {
public static void main(String[]args){
	Scanner in=new Scanner (System.in);
	int n=in.nextInt();
	int []arr=new int[n];
	for(int i=0;i<n;i++){
		arr[i]=in.nextInt();
	}
	int key=in.nextInt();
	int low=0;
	int high=n-1;
	int ans=-1;

	while(low<=high){
		int mid=(low+high)/2;
		if(arr[mid]==key){
			ans=mid;
			high=mid-1;
		}else if(key<arr[mid]){
			high=mid-1;
		}else if(key<arr[mid]){
			high=mid-1;
		}else{
			low=mid+1;
		}
	}
	if(ans!=-1){
		System.out.println(ans);
	}
	else{
		System.out.println("Not found");
	}
}

}

package q32083;
import java.util.Scanner;

public class BubbleSort {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Scanner scanner = new Scanner(System.in);

        int n = scanner.nextInt();

        int[] arr = new int[n];
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            arr[i] = scanner.nextInt();
        }

        bubbleSort(arr);

        for (int num : arr) {
            System.out.print(num + " ");
        }

        scanner.close();
    }

    public static void bubbleSort(int[] arr) {
		int n=arr.length;
		for(int i=0;i<n-1;i++){
			for(int j=0;j<n-1;j++){
				if(arr[j]>arr[j+1]){
					int temp=arr[j];
					arr[j]=arr[j+1];
					arr[j+1]=temp;
				}
			}
		}

package q22135;
import java.util.Scanner;
public class Main{
	public static void main(String[]args){
		Scanner sc=new Scanner(System.in);
		String input=sc.nextLine();
		StringBuffer sb= new StringBuffer(input);
		StringBuffer result=new StringBuffer();

		for(int i=0;i<sb.length();i++){
			char ch=sb.charAt(i);
			if(result.indexOf(String.valueOf(ch))==-1){
				result.append(ch);
			}
		}
		System.out.println(result);
	}
}

import java.util.*;
class Area{
	float side;
	float lenghth;
	float breadth;
	void Square (float side) {
		System.out.printf("Area of square for side in meters %.2f: %.4f\n", side, (side*side));
}
void Rectangle (float length, float breadth) {
System.out.printf("Area of rectangle for length and breadth in meters %.2f, %.2f: %.7f\n", length, breadth,(length*breadth));
}
}
class OverloadArea {
	public static void main(String args[]){
		Area a = new Area();
		float side = Float.parseFloat(args[0]);
		float length = Float.parseFloat(args[0]);
		float breadth=Float.parseFloat(args[1]);
		a.Square(side);
		a.Rectangle(length,breadth);
}
}

Methods:

  • compute(): To calculate the total and average marks.

class Student{

		this.cppMarks=cppMarks;

}
class Result extends Marks{
	float total;

		avg=total/3;
	}

		System.out.println("Total : "+total);
		System.out.println("Avg : "+avg);
	}
}

S.No: 12 Exp. Name: Areas of Shapes Using Abstract Class Date: 2026-08-28
Aim:

Design an abstract class named Shape to represent geometric shapes. The Shape class should declare the following abstract methods:

  • double calculateArea(): Calculates and returns the area of the shape.
  • double calculatePerimeter(): Calculates and returns the perimeter of the shape.

In addition, implement a concrete method named displayDetails() that displays the area and perimeter of the shape. Create a subclass named Circle that extends the Shape class.


The Circle class should:

  • Store the radius of the circle.
  • Implement the calculateArea() method to calculate and return the area of the circle.
  • Implement the calculatePerimeter() method to calculate and return the perimeter (circumference) of the circle.


Input Format:

  • The first line reads an integer representing the radius of the circle on the same line after the prompt:
Enter the radius of the circle: <radius>


Output Format:

  • The output displays the details of the circle in the following format:
Shape details:
Area: <area>
Perimeter: <perimeter>


Note:

  • Use Math.PI as the value of π while calculating the area and perimeter of the circle.
  • A partial code is provided in the editor. Complete the given code by implementing the required logic.
Source Code:
ID: 25B01A1279 Page No:
Shri Vishnu Engineering College for Women (Autonomous) 2025-2029-IT-B
Circle.java
import java.util.Scanner;
abstract class Shape {
	abstract double calculateArea();
	abstract double calculatePerimeter();
	public void displayDetails(){
		System.out.println("Shape details:");
		System.out.println("Area: " +calculateArea());
		System.out.println("Perimeter: " +calculatePerimeter());
	}
}
class Circle extends Shape {
    double radius;
    public Circle(double radius) {
        this.radius = radius;
    }
    @Override
 public double calculateArea() {
    	return Math.PI*radius*radius;
    }
    @Override
 public double calculatePerimeter() {
		return 2*Math.PI*radius;
    }
    
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Scanner scanner = new Scanner(System.in);
        System.out.print("Enter the radius of the circle: ");
        double radius = scanner.nextDouble();
        Circle circle = new Circle(radius);
        circle.displayDetails();
        scanner.close();
    }
}

abstract class Shape {

S.No: 20 Exp. Name: Producer Consumer Concept Date: 2026-11-01
Aim:

Write a Java program using synchronized threads, which demonstrates producer consumerconcept.


The Producer-Consumer problem is a classic synchronization problem in computer science. It involves two types of threads:

  • Producer: This thread generates data (e.g., items) and places it in a shared resource (like a buffer).
  • Consumer: This thread takes data (items) from the shared resource for processing or consumption.


The problem revolves around coordinating these threads such that:

  • The producer does not produce when the buffer is full.
  • The consumer does not consume when the buffer is empty.
  • Both threads operate safely without corrupting the shared resource.


To achieve synchronization in Java, we can use the synchronized keyword along with wait and notify methods to control the interaction between the threads.


Input Format:

  • Prompt the user to enter an integer representing the number of items to produce along with a print statement "Enter the number of items to produce: "


Output Format:

Output should print the following:

  • Messages indicating the production of each item as <Produced: {Produced item}>
  • Messages indicating the consumption of each item as <Consumed: {Consumed item}>

package q28802;
import java.util.LinkedList;
import java.util.Scanner;

// Write your code here...


public class ProducerConsumerDemo {
	// Write your code here...
	static class SharedBuffer{
		private final LinkedList<Integer> buffer = new 
		LinkedList<>();
		public synchronized void produce(int item) throws InterruptedException{
			buffer.add(item);
			System.out.println("Produced: "+item);
			notifyAll();
		}
		public synchronized void consume() throws InterruptedException{
			if(!buffer.isEmpty()){
				int item=buffer.removeFirst();
				System.out.println("Consumed: "+item);
				notifyAll();
			}
		}
	}
	public static void main(String[] args){
		Scanner sc=new Scanner(System.in);
		System.out.print("Enter the number of items to produce: ");
		int n=sc.nextInt();
		SharedBuffer sb=new SharedBuffer();
		try{
			for(int i=1;i<=n;i++){
				sb.produce(i);
				sb.consume();
			}
		}
		catch(InterruptedException e){Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
									 }
			}

package q19;
class MyThread implements Runnable{
	public void run(){
		try{
			for(int i=0;i<5;i++){
				if(Thread.currentThread().getName().equals("Thread-0"))
					System.out.println("Good Morning");
				else if(Thread.currentThread().getName().equals("Thread-1"))
					System.out.println("Hello");
				else
					System.out.println("Welcome");
				Thread.sleep(500);
			}
		}
		catch(InterruptedException e){
			System.out.println(e);
		}
	}
	public static void main(String a[]){
		MyThread obj = new MyThread();
		Thread t1 = new Thread(obj);
		Thread t2 = new Thread(obj);
		Thread t3 = new Thread(obj);
		t1.start();
		t2.start();
		t3.start();
	}
}

Create a Java program that demonstrates the use of user and daemon threads. Implement a class WorkerThread that extends Thread and overrides the run method to simulate some work by printing messages and sleeping for a short duration.


In the DaemonThread class:

1. Prompt the user to input the number of user threads and daemon threads.

2. Create and start the specified number of user threads and daemon threads.

  • User Threads: These threads will run to completion and are not interrupted by the main thread.Daemon Threads: These threads will run in the background and may be terminated abruptly when the main thread exits.

3. The main thread should print a message indicating its exit after creating the threads.


Input Format:

  • The second line contains an integer specifying the number of daemon threads.

  • Messages indicating the start and finish of each daemon thread.
  • A message indicating that the main thread is exiting as: "Main thread exiting".


Note:

  • Ensure that daemon threads are correctly set using setDaemon(true) before calling start().

import java.util.Scanner;

class WorkerThread extends Thread {
	private int threadId;
	WorkerThread(int id){
		this.threadId=id;
	}
	public void run(){
		System.out.println("Thread "+threadId+" started");
		try{
			for(int i=0;i<2;i++){
				Thread.sleep(200);
			}
			System.out.println("Thread "+threadId+" finished");
		}
		catch(InterruptedException e){
			System.out.println("Thread"+threadId+"interrupted:"+e);
		}
	}
}

public class DaemonThread {
	public static void main(String[] args) {
        Scanner scanner = new Scanner(System.in);

        System.out.print("Enter the number of user threads: ");
        int numUserThreads = scanner.nextInt();

        System.out.print("Enter the number of daemon threads: ");
        int numDaemonThreads = scanner.nextInt();
		int id=1;
		for(int i=0;i<numUserThreads;i++){
			WorkerThread userThread=new WorkerThread(id++);
			userThread.start();
		}
		id=1;
		for(int i=0;i<numDaemonThreads;i++){
			WorkerThread daemonThread=new WorkerThread(id++);
			daemonThread.setDaemon(true);
			daemonThread.start();
		}

class FirstThread extends Thread {

public class Arithmetic{
	public static int add(int a,int b){
		return a+b;
	}
	public static int subtract(int a,int b){
		return a-b;
	}
	public static int multiply(int a,int b){
		return a*b;
	}
	public static double divide(int a,int b){
		return(double)a/b;
	}
}
